messages.subject: problem in labelling bootstrap values
messages.body_plain:
Dear Developer,

Your package 'ggtree' is useful, but I still got some problem with it. Comparing the visualization result using your package and figtree, I found differences in the bootstrap labelling (an important node was marked with a red arrow in the attached file). Furthermore, the phenomenon was only observed in part of the nodes. Our tree was rerooted with the same branch in both the two tools

So far we cannot tell which one should be reliable, but here we still ask for your explanation about the unusual problem.

Best,
Tzu-Hao Kuo
Biodiversity Research Center, Academia Sinica

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

Does the gheatmap function only support matrices with categorical data?
I've been trying to use the function with a numerical matrix (making sure the row names coincide with the tree's tip labels) and get the following error:

> gheatmap(p1, mat_data, offset = 2, width=0.5)
Error: is.character(x) is not TRUE
In addition: Warning message:
In gheatmap(p1, mat_data, offset = 2, width = 0.5) : Coercing LHS to a list

Is there a way around this?

Kind regards,
Maria

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Thanks for your prompt reply. Find attached the input data, and my R script below.

> setwd("~/Desktop")
> data<-read.csv("mat_data.csv") #read mat_data file from Desktop
> rownames_mat<- data[,1]
> mat_data<- as.matrix(data[,-1])
> rownames(mat_data)<-rownames_mat
>
> tree<- read.tree("myco_newick.nwk") #read newick file from Desktop
> p1<- ggtree(tree, color="firebrick", size=1, linetype="dotted")
> p1
> gheatmap(p1, mat_data, offset = 2, width=0.5) #append tree to heatmap

Kind regards,
